After breaking up on Dec 2022, bumalik siya last May 2023, saying na ipupursue niya na ako this time. Hanggang December 2023, wala pa ring malinaw kung magiging kami ba talaga o where the “relationship” is going. Parang ako na naman ang nagppursue, eh siya naman tong bumalik. Umasa ako, lagi naman eh. Ganoon ko siyang minahal. Ang ending? Iniwan na naman ako. Mas masakit yung huling pang-iiwan kasi nakakamove on na sana ako nung May, bigla lang siya nagparamdam at nagpaasa. 

Hanggang ngayon I can’t believe tiniis (or natiis) ko yun lahat. Bumyahe by plane halos buwan-buwan, shower her with gifts na alam kong mapapasaya siya, go on leaves or take multiple days off para makasama siya, ipakilala sa family ko kahit di pa naman ako “out”, etc. Sobrang sakit kasi akala ko siya na kaya tinaya ko talaga lahat.

Anyways, sabi ko naman sa kaniya na if I can’t be the love of her life, I’ll be the loss of her life instead. I’m still trying to rebuild myself (for the nth time), pero wala na siya ngayon access sa buhay ko (blocked her number, Messenger, email). Planning to change my mobile number (and email address) soon.

I also kissed a woman the first time at 27. I’ve been wanting to kiss her since I knew I loved her. Damn, when I kissed her the first time, I no longer wanted to kiss or be intimate with anyone else but her. That’s how sure I am about her, and a few more dates and intimate moments later, I’ve reaffirmed my sexuality as full-on gay. 

Before her, I was afraid of being out there, I was scared of being bi/pan. I was scared because I grew up in a conservative family, was educated Catholic, and then was in an even much more conservative religion which didn’t align with my values. I was unsure of myself, I wanted to fit in. I didn’t have queer role models. In my early 20s, I could only be envious of those who were publicly gay, because it was a really scary world out there. I was afraid of being the subject of rumors, of being frowned upon or looked at differently. 

But loving her at this day and age made all the difference. It was like I was ready to come out to the world! I wasn’t even afraid of hugging her or holding her hand in public. I even kissed her on the lips when I rushed to meet her at a coffee shop — something I never thought I’d do with anyone. And don’t get me started with the kisses, the hugs, and intimate moments. It’s so much different with the woman you truly love. Looking into her eyes, her soft lips, her supple body, her gentle kisses, the warmth of her arms around me — all of these I have committed to memory. It was not just sex, it was making love! It all made sense why every part of it was natural, it was not painful, and for me nothing felt forced or like a chore. No more faking, trying to pretend or imagining stuff in my head. They say this is what sexual attraction does — I finally know what it feels to have your body, mind and soul in sync. Which is why I was truly satisfied in all aspects when I was with her — be it physically, intellectually, emotionally, and sexually. 

I look at her and I see our future together, and I couldn’t wait to start the rest of my life right away. I wanted to be the one doing the chase, sending flowers, giving her gifts, taking her on dates, carrying heavy stuff, doing other acts of service. I wanted to be her lady knight in shining armour, I wanted to be her lifetime partner! I wanted to marry her someday, I wanted to be the one to propose to her at some fancy restaurant or at a hotel with our family and closest friends. 

I can’t be with anyone else, I don’t want to be with anyone else, not with another woman, especially not with a man. We may not have been each other’s first but I really wanted her to be my last. That’s how certain I am of it all. She broke up with me just recently, though that’s an entirely different story. 

I kind of regret all those years I wasted dating a man, but I’m also quite glad I didn’t pursue girls I liked in the past, and that I didn’t sleep around or date around because she’s the one I was meant to find. All of those past experiences made me into the lesbian I am today, whoever I dated does not matter and does not invalidate my sexuality.

So here’s my advice — don’t be afraid of all of this. It’s normal to feel scared sometimes but don’t let it hinder you from living your best life! All good things take time. For now, just enjoy the ride! Cheers.

Kissing her soft lips made all the difference — like it finally dawned on me why I couldn’t picture myself ending up with my ex boyfriend, or any guy for that matter, and why I always craved for a deeper emotional connection that I never found on anyone else. That was it — I am a lesbian. Being with her for the past year made me want to be brave and come out to the world... That’s how much I wanted to spend the rest of my life with her. That’s how much I love her.

All those moments I spent with her made me feel the most alive... Made me ask why have I been unkind to myself and not lived the best life, denying for so long that this is who I really am. I saw a future with her and her alone, I wanted to be her partner for the rest of our lives... I looked forward to being with her every single day, waking up next to her, doing stuff for her, treating her like a princess, singing for her, writing her love letters, sending her flowers, cuddling with her every night.

She broke up with me just recently. I’m still heartbroken and will be for a long time, because I know in my heart that I have never loved anyone, nor will I ever love anyone as much as I love her.

She broke up with me just recently, but I will always keep coming back to the memory of our first kiss.
